title: Uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of embedded surface mean-curvature flow
main_claim: At every singular point at the first singular time of the MCF of a smooth closed embedded surface in R^3, the fixed-center rescalings converge locally smoothly, with multiplicity one, to a single self-shrinker sqrt(-s)S in the original ambient frame (no mean-convexity, no prescribed model). The proof uses a Lojasiewicz route through a finite-jet formal Gaussian action F(b,x). Formal critical arcs with nonzero cylindrical opening x are excluded by a contradiction: a nonzero Stokes jump G+ - G- ~ c0·sum Z*^{-2} e^{-Z*^2/4}, coming from the complex radial translator, against a Watson/Phragmen-Lindelof upper bound O(e^{-1.25 A_lead}). A real Nullstellensatz/Artin argument then gives a finite power, followed by a localized gradient inequality and a finite rescaled-length bootstrap.

issues.description: The finite conical/cylindrical end decomposition and bounded geometry are taken from citations (BK2024 Thm 1.10 and Claim 7.6, v3 numbering). I could not check them against the source offline. The paper itself notes that Wang's theorem would not apply, because finite genus does not give finite topology, so the result depends entirely on this BK statement.
issues.evidence: 'Their Theorem~1.10 gives the finite conical/cylindrical end decomposition.' 'Bounded geometry ... follows from ... the proof of the end theorem [BK2024, Claim 7.6]'

coverage:
This was a partial read, aimed at the parts the earlier sibling pass had left unverified. Checked in detail:
- jump.tex: the d0 ODE and its integral formula (sympy), the expansion d0 = 2 log r + d*, the log-height equation, the rescaled height equation → radial translator h''/(1+h'^2)+h'/y=1, the physical-action substitution, and the translator matching h=y^2/2-log y.
- Stokes lemma: the q-equation (sympy), the b_n recurrence against the formal series (sympy, n≤10), the factorial bounds, the inverse-Laplace/Borel/Pringsheim nonvanishing argument, the slope-difference coefficient -y+3/y giving c0 y^3 e^{-y^2/2}, and the boundary-momentum net comparison → c0.
- arrays.tex: the geometric-telescoping Gevrey lemma (order 1/k in s, so flatness is exp(-c/|a|), the variable the Watson-type sector argument needs), the regular implicit solve, the Phragmen-Lindelof flatness upgrade line by line, and the 1.4/1.25/1.2 margin logic in the action upper bound.
- flow.tex: the radius induction and the finite-length good/bad index summation (concavity cases and the role of kappa>1).
- geometry.tex: the representative-equality lemma.
Not verified: linear.tex / finite-linear.tex / gauges.tex inverse and gauge estimates (~2500 lines), compatibility of the height families, existence of the contour lemma, the phase section (checked by the sibling), and the BK2024 citations.
